newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose slightly to 1.003 billion yuan from 968 million yuan with the 7-day contract the most actively traded.
Dealers said trading was slow with most financial institutions remaining on the sidelines.
Reports that the inflation rate would be controlled under four percent for this year prompted talk of strong calls to cut bank reserve ratios and interest rates.
"The interbank market rates will fall if inflation rates go down," one trader said. "This made most financial institutions reluctant to trade actively."
But demand for funds to underwrite state purchase of the record summer grain harvest would continue to give support to the rates in the short-term, traders said.
Rates were seen moving marginally in the short term, they said.
